verdict.rationale: JumpCloud's own docs describe a cloud RADIUS service that authenticates users to Wi-Fi, VPNs, switches and other network devices, which covers the VPN and Wi-Fi half of the story. Nothing in the pack mentions a cloud LDAP endpoint for older systems; 'alternative to legacy AD' is directory positioning, not an LDAP capability. missing for 10: cloud LDAP endpoint evidence, legacy-system LDAP binding, independent or hands-on corroboration of RADIUS.

support.subject: As an IT admin, legacy protocols still work — cloud LDAP and RADIUS endpoints serve the VPNs, Wi-Fi, and older systems that will never speak SAML

citations.quote: support RADIUS throughout your organization to securely authenticate users to Wi-Fi, VPNs, switches, and other network devices with minimal in-house management
Simply point your Wi-Fi networks and VPNs to JumpCloud’s RADIUS servers, and easily grant secure access via your directory.
